findings.title: Scenario count claim disagrees with spec (and with design.md count)
findings.recommendation: tasks.md:55 says '7 new scenarios covering happy path + 6 edge cases' (=13); design.md:105 says '6+ new scenarios cover happy path + 5 edge cases' (=11); spec.md has 10 total scenarios (2 baseline-equivalent + 8 net-new). Reconcile to a single accurate count across the three artifacts — e.g., 'eight new scenarios (1 happy path + 7 edge cases)' in both task 3.3 and design.md risks bullet.

findings.title: Markers-precede-discovery rule is implicit, not codified
findings.recommendation: Spec has two adjacent scenarios ('Change-name positional scope with markers found' L17-20 and '...with no markers — auto-discovers internal JSON' L22-25). The precedence rule (markers grep MUST run BEFORE discovery; markers-found short-circuits discovery) is implied by their juxtaposition but never stated as a MUST. design.md D-priority-1 (L41-49) makes this explicit but it lives only in design. Add one sentence to the modified requirement summary at L5 (or a brief 'Discovery priority order' sentence in the markers-found scenario) so the spec self-contains the precedence rule and codegen reads it without cross-referencing design.md.

findings.title: Tie-break for identical filename TS tokens not specified
findings.recommendation: D-recency-1 says 'single global most-recent across both candidate types' by lexical sort of the filename <TS> token. The 'Multiple JSON candidates resolved by recency' scenario (L38-40) does not address the (rare) collision case where a review-<mode>-<TS>.json and an audit-drift-<TS>.json share an identical <TS> token (e.g., emitted in the same second). Add one sentence: 'When two candidates share an identical <TS> token, stable sort by filename string (audit-drift sorts before review-proposal which sorts before review-system) — deterministic tie-break, no AskUserQuestion.' Edge case; SUGGESTION not WARNING.

findings.title: Path-vs-change-name disambiguation rule not specified in spec
findings.recommendation: The 'Scoped scan — path or pattern' scenario (L12-15) says '(NOT a recognized change name)' but doesn't specify the heuristic for distinguishing a path argument from a change name. design.md D-discovery-1 says 'resolves to an existing change directory at openspec/changes/<name>/ or openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<name>/' — that rule is the disambiguation, but it's spec-implicit only. Consider adding one sentence to the modified requirement summary at L5: 'A positional argument is treated as a change name if it resolves to an existing directory at openspec/changes/<name>/ OR openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<name>/; otherwise it is treated as a path/pattern.' Closes the codegen ambiguity.

findings.title: Task 2.4 modifies an enum in a reference doc; consider whether the resolution-log emission contract is fully captured
findings.recommendation: Task 2.4 extends the run-summary-schema reference doc's `source` enum from `'whole-repo' | 'scope' | 'from-file'` to add `'auto-discovered'`. The spec scenario at L45 mentions this (`source` field as `'auto-discovered'`), so the contract IS declared.
